clue.text: Sable in time could become of immeasurable value

indicators.note: says the letters of these three words can be turned into something else by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Some sable fur, given enough years, might turn out to be priceless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could become' rearranges SABLE IN TIME, all eleven letters, into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Something too precious to be measured or valued is beyond estimate.

clue.text: Disposed on the tip

explanation.surface: Someone is willing, or something is tilted over.
explanation.definitionFit: Disposed means willing or leaning towards something; on the tip means tilted, sloping at an angle.

clue.text: Outrageous behaviour more than usual seen at heart of Test

parts.note: an excess is an amount more than is usual or needed

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central letters, here taken from the word Test

explanation.surface: Wild conduct beyond the norm witnessed in the middle of a cricket Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart of' takes ES, the middle two letters of TEST. A Test is an international cricket match.
explanation.definitionFit: Indulgence and outrageous conduct going beyond proper limits are known as such, plural noun.

clue.text: He takes away but could be taken in

definitions.text: He takes away but could be taken in

parts.words: He takes away but could be taken in
parts.note: a person who removes others' property and who might in turn be arrested by the police, 'taken in' meaning detained

explanation.surface: Someone who removes things but might himself be removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' reads as fooled, but it means arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: A robber removes possessions and is liable to be arrested by police.

clue.text: Possibly claimed boss at hospital department was once one

indicators.note: suggests the letters of claimed might possibly be arranged otherwise

parts.note: a boss is a raised stud, as on a shield
ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital

explanation.surface: A senior hospital consultant claims that once upon a time they trained there too.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' rearranges CLAIMED. The definition leans on the boss in the surface: a senior doctor was once a trainee.
explanation.definitionFit: Every qualified doctor once trained as a pupil at medical school before practising.

clue.text: Buoyant system to prevent low fliers

definitions.text: Buoyant system to prevent low fliers

parts.words: Buoyant system to prevent low fliers
parts.note: describes a wartime defence of tethered floating gasbags strung with cables to stop enemy aircraft flying in low

explanation.surface: A floating scheme to keep aircraft from coming in too low.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Second World War, cities were protected by rows of tethered gas-filled envelopes whose cables deterred dive-bombers.
explanation.definitionFit: Floating tethered gasbags formed a defensive screen against low-flying enemy aircraft.

clue.text: Meet with 'orse ridden by English corporal perhaps

indicators.note: in a down answer the horse sits below its riders, so it comes after them

parts.note: a corporal is an example of an NCO, a non-commissioned officer
a Cockney-style dropped H turns a hunter, a horse, into 'unter

explanation.surface: A Cockney invitation to come and see a horse ridden by an English soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'orse signals a dropped H: the horse is a (h)unter, written UNTER.
explanation.definitionFit: To meet someone is to come across them, often unexpectedly.

clue.text: Gorge some chocolate

indicators.note: only some of the letters of the word chocolate are taken, a run inside it

explanation.surface: An instruction to stuff oneself with a bit of chocolate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gorge' looks like a verb, eat greedily; it is the noun, a mountain pass.
explanation.definitionFit: A col is a pass or dip between mountain peaks, a kind of gorge.

clue.text: Pick "First Class"

explanation.surface: A label marking the best selection.
explanation.definitionFit: A pick is a selection made; first class describes something excellent or select.

clue.text: The gloss on a poor result

indicators.note: a poor version of the word result is one badly formed, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Putting a positive spin on a bad outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges the six letters of RESULT.
explanation.definitionFit: Lustre is the shine or sheen on a polished surface.

clue.text: Succulent plants put on a show in the islands

indicators.note: the performing word goes inside the islands' letters

parts.note: CI is the Channel Islands
to act is to perform or put on a show

explanation.surface: Juicy plants that are staged in an island show.
explanation.walkthrough: CI stands for the Channel Islands, British islands off the French coast.
explanation.definitionFit: These spiny desert plants store water in fleshy stems, making them succulents.

clue.text: Clue I do is surprisingly pleasing!

indicators.note: the letters of Clue I do is are arranged in a surprising new order

explanation.surface: A setter delighted to find the clue they wrote is a treat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surprisingly' rearranges CLUE I DO IS, nine letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something delightful to taste or experience is very pleasing.

clue.text: Thereby pact is of nothing if rewritten

indicators.note: the letters of the phrase are written out again in a new order

parts.note: O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: An agreement becomes void once it is redrafted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rewritten' rearranges PACT IS OF, then O for nothing is added; 'if' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means by that very fact, hence thereby.

clue.text: Part of unsure clue brought back is a source of pain

indicators.note: the portion taken is then read in the reverse direction
only a portion of the words unsure clue is taken

explanation.surface: A doubtful clue that returns is a pain for the solver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Part of' takes RECLU from unsuRE CLUe and 'brought back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: An open sore in the stomach or mouth is a painful lesion.

clue.text: One such to another one suggests close confrontation

definitions.text: One such to another one suggests close confrontation

parts.words: One such to another one suggests close confrontation
parts.note: the phrase formed by putting this organ of sight to another one describes a face-to-face standoff

explanation.surface: A riddle about a phrase used for tense head-to-head meetings.
explanation.walkthrough: The expression 'X to X' means a direct, close confrontation.
explanation.definitionFit: The globe of the organ of sight, which in the idiom meets another in a standoff.

clue.text: House planner no use in move for one employed with the herd

indicators.note: the letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: the letters of use are removed from house planner first, as 'no use' says

explanation.surface: An architect with no use for a move among the cattle.
explanation.walkthrough: Take USE from HOUSE PLANNER, leaving HOPLANNER, which 'in move' rearranges. The long wooden horn is used by Alpine herdsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: A long wooden horn played by Swiss herdsmen to call cattle.

clue.text: Catches seen in cricket practice

explanation.surface: Holding balls during a cricket training session.
explanation.definitionFit: To net is to catch, as with fish; nets are enclosed practice pitches where cricketers train.

clue.text: Diplomacy includes one on vessel saying little

indicators.note: in a down answer the first part sits on top of the second
the diplomacy word contains the numeral

parts.note: tact is diplomacy or sensitivity in dealing with people
I is the Roman numeral one
an urn is a vase or vessel

explanation.surface: A tactful sailor aboard ship who speaks little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' and 'on' are both placement signals; 'vessel' tempts a ship reading, but it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserved, uncommunicative person says very little.

clue.text: Southern town to give information to get forage stuff

parts.note: Rye is a town in East Sussex in southern England
to grass is British slang for informing to the police

explanation.surface: A south-coast town informer collects animal feed.
explanation.walkthrough: RYE is a small historic town in East Sussex; to GRASS is British slang for informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A grass grown as fodder, cut for grazing livestock.

clue.text: At university turning in larger than usual composition

indicators.note: the turned word goes inside the outsize abbreviation

parts.note: OS is outsize, larger than usual clothing

indicators.note: the university word is turned round

parts.note: up means at university, as in up at Oxford

explanation.surface: A student back at university writes a bigger piece than expected.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'up' at a university is British usage; 'turning' makes PU. OS (outsize) is a clothing size label.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical work is numbered as an opus by its composer.

clue.text: See 4
Grant set down to include arts body

indicators.note: the burial word takes the arts body inside it

parts.note: to bury is to set down in the ground
RSA is the Royal Society of Arts

explanation.surface: Funding settled to cover an arts organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: RSA is the Royal Society of Arts, a British institution.
explanation.definitionFit: A bursary is a grant of money to fund a student's studies.

clue.text: See 5
Place of worship for a group of printers?

explanation.surface: Asking whether a church could house printers.
explanation.walkthrough: A local branch of a printers' trade union was traditionally called by this church name.
explanation.definitionFit: A small church for prayer; also a printers' union branch in a workplace.

clue.text: Fervent study in paintings

indicators.note: the study goes inside the paintings

parts.note: art means paintings
a den is a private room or study

explanation.surface: Keen study of works of art.
explanation.definitionFit: Passionate and zealous, burning with enthusiasm.

clue.text: Wader seen swimming in Rhone?

indicators.note: letters of Rhone move about as if swimming

explanation.surface: A long-legged bird seen bathing in a French river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swimming' rearranges RHONE, the French river.
explanation.definitionFit: A long-legged fishing bird that stands in shallow water, a type of wading bird.

clue.text: Joining university for English could be one's undoing?

indicators.note: one letter stands in for the other

parts.note: enrolling means joining, signing up

explanation.surface: Signing up for university instead of English might ruin a student.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap U for E in ENROLLING. 'Undoing' is meant as unwinding a scroll, not ruin.
explanation.definitionFit: Unwinding a rolled scroll or bandage is literally its undoing.

clue.text: Lines about the period arising, permitted by law

indicators.note: in a down answer, arising means read upwards, so the whole is reversed
the lines go around the period

parts.note: L is a line, so lines are LL
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Writing about the era that has emerged as allowed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts AGE between the two Ls, making LAGEL, and 'arising' reverses it in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: Allowed under statute; lawful.

clue.text: Unusual appearances of people in heap on ground

indicators.note: the people go inside the rearranged letters
heap and on are ground up into new order

parts.note: men means people

explanation.surface: Strange figures of people lying on a pile on the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ground' rearranges two words into PHENOA; 'on ground' looks like a location but 'on' is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Remarkable occurrences or sights, things that are observed.

clue.text: Work with universal lawyer in 29 town

parts.note: to go means to work, as a machine goes
U is the film rating for universal
DA is a district attorney, an American lawyer

explanation.surface: Taking a job with a lawyer in a Dutch town.
explanation.walkthrough: 29 refers to the answer at 29-across, a European country.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in the south Netherlands, famous for cheese.

clue.text: Set fire to half test paper

indicators.note: only the first half of the testing word is taken

parts.note: litmus is paper used to test for acidity

explanation.surface: Burning half an exam paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Litmus paper turns red in acid and blue in alkali; half of it gives three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Ignited, as a fire or a match.

clue.text: New number arrives in Europe?

parts.note: read as numb-er, something that numbs: ether is an anaesthetic
lands means arrives

explanation.surface: A fresh figure turns up in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number' is not a figure but a numbing agent, an anaesthetic.
explanation.definitionFit: A European country, the land of dykes and tulips.
